plan: [This auction is effectively a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest sealed bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy and maximizes expected profit. There's only one round and values are independent, so no benefit to shading. I will bid my private value of $31. Ties are random; this does not change truth-telling optimality.]

[This auction functions like a second-price (pay the second-highest sealed bid) game. Truthful bidding is a dominant strategy: bid my private value ($6). There is no history to exploit and values are independent, so bidding 6 maximizes expected surplus, avoids the winner's curse from overbidding, and preserves winning whenever the price paid (second-highest bid) is below my value.]

[Since my private value is $0, I should avoid winning because any positive price yields negative payoff. In the clock stage, bidding 0 makes me exit immediately and prevents winning. Even if ties occur, a win would pay the second-highest bid—likely 0—so payoff is at best zero. Bid 0.]
